newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Syrian mothers visit sons in Israeli jails.
newsitem.headline: Syrian mothers visit sons in Israeli jails.

text.p: Four Syrian mothers crossed three countries to visit their sons jailed in Israel, an Israeli prisons spokeswoman said on Thursday.
"Yesterday there was a visit by four Syrian mothers who had requested to visit their sons held in two prisons in southern Israel," she told Reuters.
"They came through Jordan from Syria to enter Israel," she said. "The visit took place after receiving permission from a host of government offices."
The spokeswoman said there are a few Syrians scattered throughout Israel's prisons who are serving sentences for security offences and illegal entry to the Jewish state.
Israel and Syria, which have fought three major wars in the last half century, have no diplomatic relations and are formally in a state of war. Israel and Jordan signed a treaty in 1994.
